info.name: DisplacementFX
info.comment: Applies the displacement map filter effect.

description.p: Each output pixel samples FilterEffect.Input at its own position plus a displacement taken from FilterEffect.Mix or VectorMap. For a colour map, the X and Y components are the selected channels in the range 0 to 1, minus NeutralX and NeutralY respectively. Multiply the components by ScaleX and ScaleY, transform the resulting vector with the client, and add it to the output position to obtain the input sample position.

The filter colour space applies to the RGB components of FilterEffect.Mix. Alpha is read unchanged and colour channels are read in straight-alpha form. The source image is sampled in its own colour space with alpha-weighted bilinear interpolation by default.

A normal map supplied directly by LightingFX with type NORMAL is read as signed data. Select red for X and green for Y. A component of 128, or a transparent normal-map pixel, gives zero displacement along that axis. Set NormalConvention to read normal maps from other sources, such as ImageFX.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.

field.name: EdgeMode
field.comment: Controls how FilterEffect.Input is sampled outside its image region.

description.p: TRANSPARENT is the default. The SVG extension kotuku:edgeMode accepts transparent, clamp, repeat and mirror.

field.name: NeutralX
field.comment: The X channel value that gives zero displacement in a colour map.

description.p: The range is 0 to 1, with a default of 0.5. The value is in the filter colour space for RGB and in unit coverage for alpha. The SVG attribute is kotuku:neutralX.

field.name: NeutralY
field.comment: The Y channel value that gives zero displacement in a colour map.

description.p: The range is 0 to 1, with a default of 0.5. The value is in the filter colour space for RGB and in unit coverage for alpha. The SVG attribute is kotuku:neutralY.

field.name: NormalConvention
field.comment: Reads the Mix input as a normal map in the given axis convention.

description.p: The default, AUTO, reads the Mix input as a normal map only if it is the result of LightingFX with type NORMAL, and as colour otherwise. Y_DOWN and Y_UP read any Mix input as a normal map: the red, green and blue channels are signed components centred on 128, read as data in either filter colour space, and transparent pixels give zero displacement. Y_UP negates the green component, for maps whose Y increases upwards, as in OpenGL. Use the same value as LightingFX.NormalConvention so that refraction and shading agree. The alpha channel, if selected, is always read as colour. RGB normal components ignore the neutral fields.
In normal map mode a signed component of +127 displaces by half the effective scale for its axis.
The SVG attribute is kotuku:normalConvention, with the values auto, y-down and y-up.

field.name: ResampleMethod
field.comment: The resample algorithm to use for transforming the source image.

description.p: Use NEIGHBOUR for nearest-neighbour sampling or BILINEAR for alpha-weighted bilinear sampling. The default is BILINEAR, also selected by AUTO. Other values return ERR::NoSupport.

This is the fallback for both axis overrides. The scale is expressed in VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits. In bounding box units, it is a fraction of the client's bounding box width for X or height for Y. The client's linear transform applies to the displacement, including rotation and shear.

field.name: ScaleX
field.comment: Overrides Scale on the X axis.

description.p: Accepts any finite signed value. A zero override disables horizontal displacement in primitive coordinates. Read or write NaN for inheritance from Scale. An explicit override serialises as kotuku:scaleX.

field.name: ScaleY
field.comment: Overrides Scale on the Y axis.

description.p: Accepts any finite signed value. A zero override disables vertical displacement in primitive coordinates. Read or write NaN for inheritance from Scale. An explicit override serialises as kotuku:scaleY.

field.name: VectorMap
field.comment: Optional earlier filter result containing two signed floating-point components per pixel.

description.p: While bound, this input takes precedence over FilterEffect.Mix and contributes to the default primitive subregion. The first and second components multiply the effective X and Y scales directly. A component of +1 thus displaces by one effective scale along its axis in primitive units. Invalid or missing samples give zero displacement. Channel selectors, colour transfer, normal conventions and colour neutral values apply only to FilterEffect.Mix. Clearing this field reactivates the colour map on the live effect. SVG serialises the active map binding, using kotuku:vectorMap for a numerical map.

field.comment: Describes the primitive using the FilterEffect.XMLDef format.

constants.comment: Axis conventions for normal maps read by LightingFX and DisplacementFX.
constants.const: DisplacementFX only. Read the map as a normal map only if it was written by LightingFX with type NORMAL, otherwise as colour.
Green encodes Y in image axes, increasing downwards. Used by DirectX and by LightingFX's NORMAL type.
Green encodes Y increasing upwards, as in OpenGL. The green component is negated when read.
The default option is chosen by the system. This will typically be BILINEAR, but slow machines may switch to nearest neighbour and high speed machines could use more advanced methods.
Uses a broad Bessel filter that can preserve detail during resampling, but is slower than the smaller-kernel methods.
Produces a similar result to BILINEAR at a slightly higher CPU cost and a marginally sharper after-effect.
Bilinear is a common algorithm that produces a reasonable quality image quickly.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result will be less sharp than SINC.
Uses a Gaussian filter that softens the result, reducing aliasing at the cost of sharp edge detail.
Uses a Kaiser-windowed filter, giving smooth interpolation with low ringing and a cost close to BILINEAR.
This well known algorithm may serve as a point of comparison for evaluating the results of other methods. It shares characteristics with SINC and BLACKMAN.
Uses a Mitchell-Netravali filter, balancing sharpness and smoothness at a cost similar to BICUBIC.
Nearest neighbour is the fastest sampler at the cost of poor quality.
Uses a quadratic filter with a modest kernel, giving smoother results than BILINEAR with limited extra cost.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result is of very good quality.

About twice as slow as BILINEAR, this method samples a 4x4 area and produces a considerably better result, and is a good choice for enlarging images without producing artifacts when contrasting colours are present.
